Subject: Fwd: ThermalIQ pricing push — need exec signoff (request)

Team — forwarding the thread with ThermalIQ. They want ~60% effective discount for a 3-year commitment if we're including private deployment. This is materially beyond the playbook. I'm proposing we consider a structured concession that meets their cost target in year 1 while protecting unit economics in subsequent years.

My proposed commercial compromise (to present on Thurs):
- Year 1: 50% effective discount on the token rate + onboarding credit equal to one month of committed spend (to offset migration costs)
- Year 2: 35% discount
- Year 3: 30% discount
- Minimum committed spend: $1.2M per year (annualized)
- No additional private deployment SLA until year 2 (we do a VPC share + dedicated SRE hours in year 1 instead)
- Early-termination: pro-rated repayment of onboarding credit only (no additional penalties)

Rationale: bridges ThermalIQ to an aggressive first-year rate but recovers margin over time. It also avoids the immediate capital cost of a full private deploy until we’ve validated run rate.

Attachments: ThermalIQ_usage_report_Q1.csv (they shared), proposed_amendment_draft.docx

Please indicate: 1) are you comfortable approving this commercially? 2) If not, what floor do you need to preserve? I need a VP/CFO response by EOD Thursday so we can present a single path on the call.

Thanks,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Lauren / Marissa — ran the numbers against their Q1 usage and our blended unit costs. Summary:
- At 60% off list, we lose ~38% margin on expected run rate (unsustainable).
- At 45% off list (your original draft), we break even after accounting for onboarding credit but only with a 3-year commitment and $1.5M annual minimum.
- The structured step-down is reasonable but I recommend tightening the floor and adding an annual true-up clause.

Recommended commercial counter (finance-friendly):
1) Year 1: 50% discount, $1.2M minimum annual commit, onboarding credit capped at $150k (recoupable over 12 months if they walk)
2) Year 2: 35% discount, minimum annual commit remains $1.2M, enable private deployment scope review
3) Year 3: 30% discount, annual true-up and consumption floor adjustment based on trailing 12-months
4) Overage rate: 10% premium to list beyond committed volume

I've attached margin_calculation_ThermalIQ.xlsx with assumptions. This preserves a workable gross margin (~18-22% over 3 years) assuming their growth profile. Legal will need to review the recoupable onboarding credit language.

If leadership approves, we can present the above on the Thursday call. If Markus needs a tighter floor (50% initial only with higher commit), call it out.

- Marcus
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
